ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows two JK flip-flops connected in cascade. The outputs of the left flip-flop are labeled Q_A and not Q_A; its J and K inputs are both connected to the high level labeled 5V, so J_A=K_A=1. The output of the right flip-flop is labeled Q_B; the not Q_A output of the left flip-flop is connected by a wire to the J and K inputs of the right flip-flop, so J_B=K_B=not Q_A. The bottom CLK line serves as the clock input. Reasoning: A JK flip-flop toggles when J=K=1, so Q_A^+=not Q_A. The problem gives the current state Q_A Q_B=00, so the old Q_A=0, the old Q_B=0, and the old not Q_A=1. Since the clock rise time is much less than the flip-flop delay, the right flip-flop uses the pre-clock not Q_A=1 at the same clock edge; therefore it is also in the toggle condition J_B=K_B=1, and Q_B^+=Q_B xor not Q_A=0 xor 1=1. At the same time Q_A^+=1. Therefore the next state Q_A Q_B=11.

method.method_draft: First describe the image connections, then write next-state equations. For flip-flop A, J_A=K_A=1, so Q_A^+=\bar Q_A. For flip-flop B, J_B=K_B=\bar Q_A, so it toggles when the old \bar Q_A=1 and holds when old \bar Q_A=0; equivalently Q_B^+=Q_B \oplus \bar Q_A using the pre-clock value. Substitute the text-given current state Q_AQ_B=00, hence \bar Q_A=1. Then Q_A^+=1 and Q_B^+=0\oplus1=1, giving next state 11.
